heading.en: What does one more tray cost?

hook.en: A bakery pays rent whether it bakes or not, but flour and gas rise with every tray. Splitting *costs* this way explains the famous U-shaped curves.

title.en: Define TFC, TVC, TC, AFC, AVC, AC and SMC
Explain the shapes of short-run cost curves

say.en: A bakery pays rent whether it bakes or not, but flour and gas rise with every tray. Splitting costs this way explains the famous U-shaped curves. In this lesson: Define TFC, TVC, TC, AFC, AVC, AC and SMC.
Calculate cost schedules.
Explain the shapes of short-run cost curves.

body.en: In the short run, total fixed cost (TFC) does not change with output (rent, interest, permanent staff) and total variable cost (TVC) rises with output (raw materials, wages of casual labour). $TC = TFC + TVC$. Per-unit costs: $AFC = TFC/q$, $AVC = TVC/q$, $AC = TC/q = AFC + AVC$. *Short-run* marginal cost is the change in total cost from one more unit: $SMC = \Delta TC/\Delta q = \Delta TVC/\Delta q$.

narration.en: Total cost is fixed cost plus variable cost. Dividing by output gives average costs, and marginal cost is the extra cost of one more unit.
narration.kn: ಒಟ್ಟು ವೆಚ್ಚ = ಸ್ಥಿರ ವೆಚ್ಚ + ಬದಲಾಗುವ ವೆಚ್ಚ. ಉತ್ಪನ್ನದಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಿದರೆ ಸರಾಸರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚಗಳು; ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಘಟಕದ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಸೀಮಾಂತ ವೆಚ್ಚ.

blocks.formula: AC = AFC + AVC,\quad SMC = \frac{\Delta TC}{\Delta q}

say.en: AC equals AFC plus AVC.
SMC equals delta TC over delta q equals delta TVC/delta q.
At q equals 0, TC equals TFC.
Fixed cost is 30 rupees. Total cost for 0 to 5 trays is 30, 50, 60, 66, 80 and 105. Subtract 30 to get TVC.
AVC is TVC over q: 20, 15, 12, 12.5, 15. AC is TC over q: 50, 30, 22, 20, 21.
MC is the change in TC: 20, 10, 6, 14, 25. MC is below AVC while AVC falls, and above it once AVC rises.
Now the smooth curves. AFC falls forever. AVC, AC and MC are U-shaped, and MC passes through the bottoms of AVC and AC.

body.en: TFC is a horizontal line; TVC starts from the origin; TC starts from the TFC level and runs parallel to TVC. AFC is a rectangular hyperbola that falls throughout. AVC, AC and SMC are U-shaped because of the law of variable proportions: as MP of the variable input rises, cost per unit falls, and as MP falls, cost per unit rises. SMC cuts AVC and AC at their minimum points. The gap between AC and AVC (= AFC) narrows as output rises, and minimum AC lies to the right of minimum AVC.

problem.en: A firm's TFC is ₹30 and its TC for 1 to 5 units is ₹50, 60, 66, 80, 105. Find TVC, AFC, AVC, AC and MC.

answer.en: AVC is lowest (₹12) at 3 units; AC is lowest (₹20) at 4 units; MC = 20, 10, 6, 14, 25.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A firm's TFC is ₹30 and its TC for 1 to 5 units is ₹50, 60, 66, 80, 105. Find TVC, AFC, AVC, AC and MC.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A firm's TFC is 30 rupees and its TC for 1 to 5 units is 50, rupees 60, 66, 80, 105. Find TVC, AFC, AVC, AC and MC.
TVC equals TC minus 30: 20, 30, 36, 50, 75.
AFC equals 30 over q: 30, 15, 10, 7.5, 6. AVC equals TVC/q: 20, 15, 12, 12.5, 15.
AC equals TC over q: 50, 30, 22, 20, 21 (check: AFC plus AVC, e.g. 7.5 plus 12.5 equals 20).
MC equals delta TC: 20, 10, 6, 14, 25.
So the answer is AVC is lowest 12 rupees at 3 units; AC is lowest 20 rupees at 4 units; MC equals 20, 10, 6, 14, 25.

body.en: The SMC curve is the elevator that passes through the lowest floor of AVC first and then of AC. AFC is the curve that never lands.
